metadata.title: Why a Dim Blue Lamp Beats a Blinding Red One
metadata.thing: the packet-electron collision at the escape cost
metadata.palette_note: Bear's call (2026-07-03, after viewing): literal RED for the low-frequency light — #FC6255 (3b1b-style red, reads on the dark canvas), overriding the series no-red rule for this video only. High-frequency stays blue #58C4DD. The layout audit checks geometry only, so this is safe.
chapters: What we skipped, and your turn
metadata.long_title: Why a Dim Blue Lamp Beats a Blinding Red One — the photoelectric effect | Bear's Notes
metadata.description_blurb: In this video: why a blinding red lamp frees no electrons while a dim blue one works instantly; light arriving as packets whose energy is set by color alone (E = hν); the all-or-nothing escape cost Φ; the leftover K = hν − Φ and the threshold frequency; and sodium by the numbers — where 300 nm succeeds and a ten-thousand-watt green lamp fails.
metadata.short_blurb: The photoelectric effect, from anomaly to E = hν. Full explainer on the channel.
